appended_text: PMID:10913096 additionally reports that pectinase-digested citrus or apple pectin increased the yiaJ/plaR-lacZ reporter 10-20-fold in ECL1, but not JA134. Structural-gene expression was unaffected even without the repressor, and the biological significance remained unresolved. Preparation: 0.14% pectin in sodium acetate, pH 4.0; overnight at 25 C with 400 U Aspergillus niger pectinase; tenfold dilution into medium. This undefined hydrolysate is retained as experimental context, without assigning an individual chemical or a PlaR-binding interaction.

evidence.source_assertion: Pectinase-digested citrus or apple pectin increased the yiaJ-lacZ reporter 10-20-fold in ECL1 but not JA134. Structural-gene expression was unaffected even without the repressor; the authors left the significance unresolved.

Pectin was prepared at 0.14% in sodium acetate at pH 4.0, digested overnight at 25 C with 400 U of Aspergillus niger pectinase, then diluted tenfold into medium. The tested hydrolysate is an undefined mixture, not an identified PlaR ligand.

representation: Undefined pectin hydrolysate condition; no named chemical, reaction, or mechanistic edge.
